patch_description: The Kalman filter's lag error (0.26) and slope changes (82.20) can be improved by adding lead compensation using the *RTS-smoothed* Kalman slope state rather than a raw gradient. The smoother already produces a denoised slope estimate (`smoothed[:, 1]`) as part of the state vector — using it is essentially free. Applying a short 5-tap moving average to this slope channel removes any residual high-frequency energy before lead compensation, so a moderately aggressive lead (0.3 × effective lag) reduces lag error without re-injecting noise or causing spurious reversals. Additionally, tightening the reversal-gate thresholds slightly (sig 1.5→1.8, innovation significance 1.0→1.2) reduces false reversals (currently 60.40) by demanding more statistical evidence before boosting process noise, at minimal cost to genuine turning-point responsiveness since the gate only *increases* agility when triggered.
